title: Guard denial after a gc-reaped worktree is indistinguishable from the normal one, and it advertises 'down --all' to a session that cannot see other workspaces
body:
Two problems that compound. Hit during a long `fr-goal` run on `derio-net/frank` (fr **3.19.0**) with three unrelated sessions live in the same repo.

## 1. A reaped worktree turns the `cd` escape into a total, unexplained lockout

`fr`'s gc reconciles merged workspaces, so once a PR merges its worktree under `~/.cache/fr/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>/` is **deleted**.

Every subsequent command of the prescribed shape then fails:

```bash
cd ~/.cache/fr/worktrees/frank/feat__blog-igpu-retrieval && git status
```

The `cd` fails (directory gone), so `fr-isolation-guard.sh` sees the session cwd still inside the base repo and denies the whole command — including a bare `ls`, `cat` or `find`. The denial is the standard message:

> fr pipeline active — ALL base-repo commands are gated (not just git/gh) … lead with `cd <worktree> && …` to work from the worktree cwd.

Which is advice the operator **is already following**. Nothing distinguishes "you forgot to cd" from "the directory you are cd-ing into no longer exists", so it reads as the guard misbehaving. It is more confusing still because the identical command worked minutes earlier, and because the pipeline stays active on *other* sessions' sentinels, so it never lifts on its own.

**Suggested fix:** when the command leads with `cd <path>` and `<path>` does not exist, say so:

> `<path>` no longer exists — an fr worktree is removed once its branch merges. Start a new workspace with `fr isolation up --branch <name>`, or `cd` into a live one (`fr isolation status`).

That one line would have saved a handful of dead-end commands.

**Related, same root:** `fr isolation verify-merge --branch <b>` fails *after* the merge it exists to verify, because the workspace is already gone:

```
error: no isolation workspace for branch 'ops/igpu-retrieval-archive'.
```

The `fr-goal` skill prescribes exactly this as step 9's first action ("**first verify it reached `main`** via `fr isolation verify-merge --branch <b>`"). If gc has already run, the tool cannot answer and the operator falls back to `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>` by hand. Worth either resolving the branch without a live workspace, or reporting "workspace already reaped; checked `origin/main` directly".

## 2. The guard advertises `down --all` unconditionally

The same message ends:

> No worktree left? `fr isolation down --all` clears the pipeline.

To an operator staring at a lockout, that is the obvious next command. But `--all` acts on **every** workspace in the repo, and a session has no visibility into how many belong to other sessions.

Correcting my own first reading, in fairness to the current design: `_down_all` is not indiscriminate.

> A workspace whose PR is still OPEN is KEPT (never silently destroyed) unless `--force` — that open-PR check is the only IsolationError `down` raises

So open-PR workspaces are protected. In my case all three concurrent workspaces had open PRs (#733, #750, #756) and would have survived.

**The gap is the pre-PR state.** A workspace that has not opened its PR yet has no shield, and plain `--all` tears it down. That is precisely the state a session occupies for most of an `fr-goal` run — mine were pre-PR for hours. So the guard's own suggestion can destroy a sibling session's in-progress workspace, including uncommitted work, with no confirmation and no listing of what it is about to remove.

### Suggestions, roughly in order of value

- **Make `--all` show its blast radius and confirm.** Print what will be torn down versus kept before acting — `2 workspaces: tearing down ops/foo (no PR); keeping feat/bar (PR #733 open)` — and require confirmation when it would remove a workspace this session did not create.
- **Extend the shield to pre-PR workspaces**, or at minimum to any workspace with a dirty tree or unpushed commits. The open-PR check protects the *least* vulnerable state and skips the most vulnerable one.
- **Stop advertising `--all` unconditionally in the guard message.** For the "no worktree left" case the right advice is nearly always `fr isolation up --branch <name>` — allowed from the base repo, since it is an `fr isolation …` command, and you usually need a branch for close-out work anyway. Reserve `--all` for the genuine orphaned-sentinel deadlock it was added for (#341), and point at `fr isolation status` first.
- Consider a narrower verb for the common case: clear only *this* session's sentinel rather than acting on every workspace in the repo.

## Environment

fr 3.19.0, macOS, `derio-net/frank`, three concurrent sessions. Guard message quoted from `hooks/fr-isolation-guard.sh:109`; `--all` semantics from `fr/commands/isolation_cmd.py::_down_all` and `fr isolation down --help`.

Possibly adjacent to #421 (cd-allowance gaps), but distinct: that one is about *other repos* being unreachable; this is about a *reaped* worktree in the same repo, plus the remedy the guard recommends for it.
